projectInfo.name: JavaScript Test Smells Research
projectInfo.description: Research project for detecting and refactoring JavaScript test smells using static analysis tools and LLM-based refactoring

context.purpose: This project focuses on identifying test smells in JavaScript test suites, refactoring them using LLMs, and comparing the results

keyDirectories.repositories: Contains ~30 cloned JavaScript repositories for analysis
keyDirectories.smells_detected: Output directory containing smell detection results for each repository
keyDirectories.smell_detection_tools: Static analysis tools (Steel, SNutsJS) for detecting test smells
keyDirectories.llm-refactor-pipeline: Python CLI tool for orchestrating LLM-based refactoring
keyDirectories.tests_output: Test execution results and coverage reports
keyDirectories.scripts: Utility scripts for analysis and comparison

testSmellTypes: Assertion Roulette - Tests with multiple assertions without clear messages
Eager Test - Tests that check too many things at once
Lazy Test - Multiple test cases in one test method
Mystery Guest - Tests that depend on external resources
Test Code Duplication - Repeated test code patterns
Unknown Test - Tests without clear assertions

workflow.detection: Use Steel or SNutsJS to detect smells in test files
workflow.refactoring: Use llm-refactor-pipeline to apply LLM-based refactoring
workflow.testing: Run Jest tests to ensure functionality is preserved
workflow.analysis: Compare smell counts and test results before/after refactoring

researchFocus.primary: Detecting and refactoring test smells in JavaScript
researchFocus.secondary: Comparing effectiveness of different refactoring approaches
metrics: Number of smells removed after refactoring

notes: This is an experimental research project
Repositories contain real open-source projects (dayjs, luxon, jasmine, etc.)
The llm-refactor-pipeline is a modular CLI tool for orchestrating the workflow
Results are tracked in CSV files and text summaries
Git history shows iterative development and testing
